verdict.rationale: Bland documents its own pre-production testing tools. Manual test chats run from the pathway editor and the testbed, which replays a node interaction and re-runs it many times. LLM-judge evals exist, and draft and staging environments keep tests away from live calls. Coverage is partial because the evals are described as grading calls rather than a pre-deployment simulation suite, and no automated simulated-caller testing is documented. missing for 10: automated simulated-caller or scenario testing at scale, explicit docs on running evals against test conversations before deployment, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can test agents with simulated conversations or evals before putting them on real phone calls

citations.quote: The testbed lets you take any call — whether it's a historical call from call logs or a test chat from the pathway editor — isolate a specific node interaction, edit the prompt, and run it multiple times to see how the output varies.
Evals let you measure the quality of your calls with LLM judges. You define eval agents, each of which grades one dimension of a call
An evaluation is a judge reading a conversation and saying whether the agent did the thing you wanted.
You can also promote a version to staging to test it before it goes live
Every agent has three environments: development, staging and production.
